
```{r}
###############################################################################
# ssGSEA (Hallmark) for 4 patient-derived organoids (PDOs):
#   BO-046, BO-114, BO-189, BO-268
#
# INPUT   PDO_raw_counts.csv   (made by Extract_PDO_raw_counts.R)
#         gene (Ensembl ID, with version) + 4 columns of raw integer counts
#
# WORKFLOW
#   1. Read raw counts
#   2. Gene cleaning: Ensembl -> symbol, protein-coding only, one row per symbol
#      (same logic as the pILC DESeq2/ssGSEA script)
#   3. Count filter: >= MIN_COUNT counts in >= MIN_SAMPLES samples
#   4. VST on the 4 samples (blind = TRUE, no grouping used)
#   5. Variance filter: remove the bottom VAR_FILTER_PCT of genes by VST variance
#      (set VAR_FILTER_PCT <- 0 to switch it off)
#   6. ssGSEA with Hallmark gene sets (normalize = TRUE, as in the pILC script)
#   7. Sensitivity check: ssGSEA again WITHOUT the variance filter, and the
#      correlation between the two sets of scores
#   8. Tables and figures
#
# IMPORTANT NOTES
#   - ssGSEA is rank-based inside each sample. Removing genes changes the ranks,
#     so step 7 shows whether the variance filter changes the result.
#   - normalize = TRUE rescales scores by their range ACROSS THE 4 SAMPLES.
#     The scores are therefore relative within these PDOs and must NOT be
#     compared directly with scores from the pILC tumor run.
#   - With n = 4 no statistical test is possible. Results are descriptive.
###############################################################################

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(DESeq2)
  library(org.Hs.eg.db)
  library(AnnotationDbi)
  library(GSVA)
  library(ComplexHeatmap)
  library(circlize)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
})

SEED <- 42
set.seed(SEED)

# ------------------------------ 1. SETTINGS ----------------------------------
PDO_DIR      <- "/ix1/alee/LO_LAB/Personal/Rahul/pILC/RNASeq/PDO"
COUNTS_FILE  <- file.path(PDO_DIR, "PDO_raw_counts.csv")
HALLMARK_GMT <- "/ix1/alee/LO_LAB/Personal/Rahul/pILC/RNASeq/GSEA/Dataset/h.all.v2025.1.Hs.symbols.gmt"

OUT_DIR <- PDO_DIR
dir.create(file.path(OUT_DIR, "plots"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

MIN_COUNT     <- 10    # a gene must have at least this many counts ...
MIN_SAMPLES   <- 1     # ... in at least this many of the 4 samples
VAR_FILTER_PCT <- 0.10 # remove the bottom 10% of genes by VST variance (0 = off)
TOP_N         <- 10    # top pathways reported per sample

# ---------------------------- 2. READ RAW COUNTS -----------------------------
raw <- read.csv(COUNTS_FILE, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
samples <- setdiff(colnames(raw), "gene")
counts  <- as.matrix(raw[, samples])
rownames(counts) <- raw$gene
mode(counts) <- "integer"
stopifnot(!anyNA(counts), all(counts >= 0))
message("Raw count matrix: ", nrow(counts), " genes x ", ncol(counts), " samples")

# ------------------------ 3. GENE CLEANING (SYMBOLS) -------------------------
ids  <- sub("\\..*$", "", rownames(counts))        # remove Ensembl version suffix
anno <- AnnotationDbi::select(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = unique(ids),
                              keytype = "ENSEMBL",
                              columns = c("SYMBOL", "GENETYPE"))
anno   <- anno[!duplicated(anno$ENSEMBL), ]
symbol <- anno$SYMBOL[match(ids, anno$ENSEMBL)]
gtype  <- anno$GENETYPE[match(ids, anno$ENSEMBL)]

# Keep protein-coding genes that have a gene symbol
keep   <- !is.na(symbol) & symbol != "" & gtype %in% "protein-coding"
counts <- counts[keep, ]
symbol <- symbol[keep]

# Duplicated symbols: keep the row with the highest mean count
ord    <- order(rowMeans(counts), decreasing = TRUE)
counts <- counts[ord, ]
symbol <- symbol[ord]
counts <- counts[!duplicated(symbol), ]
rownames(counts) <- symbol[!duplicated(symbol)]
n_coding <- nrow(counts)
message("Protein-coding genes with symbol: ", n_coding)

# ----------------------------- 4. COUNT FILTER -------------------------------
counts <- counts[rowSums(counts >= MIN_COUNT) >= MIN_SAMPLES, ]
n_count_filt <- nrow(counts)
message("After count filter (>= ", MIN_COUNT, " counts in >= ", MIN_SAMPLES,
        " samples): ", n_count_filt)

# ------------------------------- 5. VST --------------------------------------
# design = ~ 1 and blind = TRUE: the transformation does not use any grouping
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts,
                              colData   = data.frame(sample = colnames(counts),
                                                     row.names = colnames(counts)),
                              design    = ~ 1)
vst_mat <- assay(vst(dds, blind = TRUE))

# ------------------------- 6. VARIANCE FILTER --------------------------------
gene_var <- apply(vst_mat, 1, var)
if (VAR_FILTER_PCT > 0) {
  cutoff   <- quantile(gene_var, probs = VAR_FILTER_PCT)
  vst_filt <- vst_mat[gene_var > cutoff, ]
} else {
  vst_filt <- vst_mat
}
n_var_filt <- nrow(vst_filt)
message("After variance filter (bottom ", VAR_FILTER_PCT * 100, "% removed): ", n_var_filt)

filter_summary <- data.frame(
  step  = c("Protein-coding with symbol", "After count filter", "After variance filter"),
  genes = c(n_coding, n_count_filt, n_var_filt))
write.csv(filter_summary, file.path(OUT_DIR, "PDO_gene_filtering_summary.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(vst_filt, file.path(OUT_DIR, "PDO_vst_filtered.csv"))

# ----------------------------- 7. ssGSEA -------------------------------------
# Hallmark GMT: name <tab> description <tab> genes...
gmt_lines <- strsplit(readLines(HALLMARK_GMT), "\t")
hallmark  <- setNames(lapply(gmt_lines, function(x) x[-(1:2)]),
                      sapply(gmt_lines, `[`, 1))

run_ssgsea <- function(mat) {
  sc <- gsva(ssgseaParam(exprData = mat, geneSets = hallmark, normalize = TRUE))
  rownames(sc) <- sub("^HALLMARK_", "", rownames(sc))
  sc
}

ss_scores <- run_ssgsea(vst_filt)
write.csv(ss_scores, file.path(OUT_DIR, "PDO_ssGSEA_Hallmark_scores.csv"))

# Gene-set coverage: how many genes of each Hallmark set are in the matrix
coverage <- data.frame(
  pathway   = sub("^HALLMARK_", "", names(hallmark)),
  set_size  = lengths(hallmark),
  n_found   = sapply(hallmark, function(g) sum(g %in% rownames(vst_filt))),
  row.names = NULL) %>%
  mutate(fraction_found = round(n_found / set_size, 3))
write.csv(coverage, file.path(OUT_DIR, "PDO_ssGSEA_Hallmark_gene_coverage.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
if (any(coverage$fraction_found < 0.8))
  message("Warning: pathways with < 80% of genes found: ",
          paste(coverage$pathway[coverage$fraction_found < 0.8], collapse = ", "))

# ------------------- 8. SENSITIVITY: WITH vs WITHOUT VARIANCE FILTER ---------
if (VAR_FILTER_PCT > 0) {
  ss_nofilt <- run_ssgsea(vst_mat)
  write.csv(ss_nofilt, file.path(OUT_DIR, "PDO_ssGSEA_Hallmark_scores_no_variance_filter.csv"))
  sens <- data.frame(
    sample = colnames(ss_scores),
    spearman_filtered_vs_unfiltered = sapply(colnames(ss_scores), function(s)
      cor(ss_scores[, s], ss_nofilt[rownames(ss_scores), s], method = "spearman")),
    row.names = NULL)
  write.csv(sens, file.path(OUT_DIR, "PDO_ssGSEA_variance_filter_sensitivity.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  print(sens)   # values close to 1 = the variance filter changes nothing important
}

# --------------------------- 9. TOP PATHWAYS ---------------------------------
score_long <- as.data.frame(t(ss_scores)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
  pivot_longer(-sample, names_to = "pathway", values_to = "score")

top_paths <- score_long %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  arrange(desc(score), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
  filter(rank <= TOP_N) %>%
  ungroup()
write.csv(top_paths, file.path(OUT_DIR, "PDO_ssGSEA_Hallmark_top_pathways_per_sample.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# ------------------------------ 10. FIGURES ----------------------------------
# 10a. Heatmap of raw ssGSEA scores (not z-scores: with n = 4 a z-score would
#      exaggerate small differences)
rng <- range(ss_scores)
ht <- Heatmap(ss_scores, name = "ssGSEA\nscore",
              col = colorRamp2(c(rng[1], mean(rng), rng[2]),
                               c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B")),
              cluster_columns = TRUE, cluster_rows = TRUE,
              show_column_names = TRUE,
              row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),
              column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),
              column_title = "Hallmark ssGSEA scores, PDOs")
png(file.path(OUT_DIR, "plots", "PDO_ssGSEA_Hallmark_heatmap.png"),
    width = 2200, height = 2600, res = 300)
draw(ht); dev.off()
pdf(file.path(OUT_DIR, "plots", "PDO_ssGSEA_Hallmark_heatmap.pdf"), width = 7.5, height = 8.5)
draw(ht); dev.off()

# 10b. Ranked top pathways, one plot per sample
for (s in colnames(ss_scores)) {
  d <- top_paths %>% filter(sample == s) %>%
    mutate(pathway = factor(pathway, levels = rev(pathway)))
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(score, pathway)) +
    geom_col(fill = "#B2182B", alpha = 0.8) +
    labs(title = paste0(s, ": top ", TOP_N, " Hallmark pathways"),
         x = "ssGSEA enrichment score", y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
  ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "plots", paste0("PDO_ssGSEA_top_pathways_", s, ".png")),
         p, width = 7.5, height = 5, dpi = 300)
  ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "plots", paste0("PDO_ssGSEA_top_pathways_", s, ".pdf")),
         p, width = 7.5, height = 5)
}

message("Done. Outputs in: ", OUT_DIR)
sessionInfo()
```
